description: Cursor control identifiers. Microphone, New Chat, Model Picker and Approve are native actions; Send, encoder press, Decline and model navigation are native keys; other controls use Input API Smart Actions.
notes: The bundled layer maps API identifiers on a separate Cursor layer; Microphone, New Chat, Model Picker and Approve use the native Actions below.
The unused switch beneath the wide microphone key should remain KC_NONE, avoiding two toggles from one press.
Joystick directions require Input radial sectors. Up and down send native arrow keys for the open model picker; raw analog movement is not exposed by the WebSocket API.

The Fast-labeled button is Cmd+N on macOS or Ctrl+N on Windows for New Chat. The Fork-labeled button is Cmd+/ or Ctrl+/ for the model picker. Approve is Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter, Decline is Escape, and Send is Enter. They act on Cursor's focused Agents Window.

Encoder press shares the native Enter mapping: it confirms focused menus and submits when Cursor's composer treats Enter as Send. Encoder hold has no separate action; open setup with /worklouder-setup.
Do not replace the keys on the default device layer. Use a separate layer.
Every imported Action, Multiaction and Smart Action belongs to a group named Cursor in its category. All API identifiers start with cursor.; native controls do not use API identifiers.

nativeActions.behavior: Control and M are pressed while the physical key is held and released by firmware when it is released.
Firmware sends a native Enter key while Cursor's composer is focused.
Firmware sends Cursor's native approval shortcut to the focused chat.
Firmware creates a new chat while Cursor's Agents Window is focused.
Firmware opens Cursor's native model picker while the Agents Window is focused.
Firmware moves to the previous entry while Cursor's model picker is open.
Firmware moves to the next entry while Cursor's model picker is open.
Firmware sends Cursor's native decline or skip shortcut to the focused approval UI.
